split_policy: twelve distinct scenario families per split; five independently phrased tasks per family; no family crosses the dev/holdout split

tasks.question: show the text inside a file
tasks.rationale: The pinned common cat page prints a file to standard output.

tasks.question: print a file's contents in the terminal
tasks.rationale: The selected cat example directly displays a file's contents.

tasks.question: read a file to standard output
tasks.rationale: cat's first example supplies the requested file-reading behavior.

tasks.question: display what is in this text file
tasks.rationale: The corpus includes a common cat workflow for terminal file output.

tasks.question: send a file's contents to stdout
tasks.rationale: The labeled cat example covers writing file contents to stdout.

tasks.question: copy one file to a new path
tasks.rationale: The pinned cp page has direct file-to-file and file-to-directory examples.

tasks.question: duplicate a file somewhere else
tasks.rationale: The two labeled cp examples cover copying a file to a path or directory.

tasks.question: make a copy of a source file at a target path
tasks.rationale: cp's direct file-to-file example provides the requested support.

tasks.question: copy a file into another directory
tasks.rationale: cp's file-into-directory example matches the full behavior.

tasks.question: put a duplicate of this file in a destination
tasks.rationale: Either labeled cp example performs the requested single-file copy.

tasks.question: encrypt a file with a common command
tasks.rationale: No selected common page provides a complete file-encryption workflow.

tasks.question: monitor a directory for changes continuously
tasks.rationale: The pinned common selection has no directory-watch command.

tasks.question: create a password-protected archive
tasks.rationale: The corpus does not include an archive-encryption example.

tasks.question: show the differences between two files
tasks.rationale: No selected page documents comparing two files with a diff workflow.

tasks.question: download a file over HTTP from the shell
tasks.rationale: The broader fixture has no HTTP-download page in common.

tasks.question: list failed systemd units on Linux
tasks.rationale: The Linux systemctl page explicitly lists failed units.

tasks.question: restart a Linux service with systemd
tasks.rationale: systemctl's service-control example covers restarting a Linux service.

tasks.question: check whether a systemd unit is active
tasks.rationale: The selected systemctl page documents active-unit checks.

tasks.question: show running services on a Linux machine
tasks.rationale: The first systemctl example shows running services.

tasks.question: reload systemd after changing a unit
tasks.rationale: The pinned page provides the daemon-reload workflow.

tasks.question: list network interfaces on Linux
tasks.rationale: The ip page provides detailed and brief interface listings.

tasks.question: show the Linux routing table
tasks.rationale: The ip routing example directly displays the Linux routing table.

tasks.question: display brief address information for interfaces
tasks.rationale: The brief address example covers compact interface inspection.

tasks.question: inspect the ARP neighbors on Linux
tasks.rationale: The pinned ip page includes the neighbor-table workflow.

tasks.question: see detailed network device information
tasks.rationale: The selected Linux corpus provides detailed interface inspection with ip.

tasks.question: list running processes on Linux
tasks.rationale: The pinned Linux pages contain no process-listing example.

tasks.question: change permissions on a Linux file
tasks.rationale: No selected Linux page changes file permissions.

tasks.question: mount a filesystem on Linux
tasks.rationale: The fixture has no Linux filesystem-mount workflow.

tasks.question: show per-directory disk usage on Linux
tasks.rationale: Directory-level disk usage is not covered by the selected pages.

tasks.question: terminate a Linux process by name
tasks.rationale: The pinned Linux selection has no process-termination example.

tasks.question: copy a file into the macOS clipboard
tasks.rationale: The pinned pbcopy file-input example copies a file to the macOS clipboard.

tasks.question: send command output to the Mac pasteboard
tasks.rationale: pbcopy's command-output example supports sending shell results to the pasteboard.

tasks.question: write the macOS clipboard to a file
tasks.rationale: The selected pbpaste page writes clipboard contents to a file.

tasks.question: pipe clipboard text into grep on macOS
tasks.rationale: pbpaste's pipe example supplies clipboard-to-command behavior.

tasks.question: move shell input into the Apple clipboard
tasks.rationale: The expanded macOS corpus covers shell input transfer with pbcopy.

tasks.question: convert a HEIC image to JPEG on macOS
tasks.rationale: The selected macOS pages have no image-conversion workflow.

tasks.question: connect to a Wi-Fi network from the shell on macOS

tasks.question: inspect Mac battery cycle count

tasks.question: mount a disk image on macOS
